verdict.rationale: iTerm2's own docs make AI an optional, separately installed plugin, and that separation is meant to prevent terminal data from being sent over the network by accident. The LLM chat only works with terminal contents optionally, through sessions you explicitly link. Community reports say AI is off by default and uses your own API key rather than a forced login, though some users complained that the earlier built-in version was only 'unconfigured' rather than truly toggled off. missing for 10: first-party documentation of granular per-session controls over exactly what data is sent, an explicit documented disable toggle in settings, first-party confirmation that no account or login is required, and independent verification of the plugin's network isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use or fully disable AI features with clear control over what session data leaves my machine, without a forced login

citations.quote: This is an optional component you can install to enable generative AI features in iTerm2.
It exists as a separate component to ensure that there's no way to accidentally send information from the terminal over the network.
Built-in LLM chat window that can optionally interact with terminal contents. Link sessions to get context-aware help
The AI feature isn't enabled by default and requires your own API key
